sentences.text:
Case of the appellant/claimant in brief is that on 26.02.2013, the vehicle bearing registration No.
CG-16-8724 was driven by the driver of the appellant Baboo Yadav and he was going along with his family from Baikunthpur to Janakpur.

At about 1.30 noon, in front of police station Kelhari,
respondent No.1/driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No. CG-16A-1705, driving rashly and negligently dashed it from behind as a result of which the vehicle owned by the appellant got uncontrolled and turned turtle and got damaged including the wipers, couch of the window disc and other parts.
It was further pleaded that 1,51,485/- was spent to repair the vehicle.
The total compensation of Rs. 2,51,485/- for the damages caused was claimed by the appellant.
The respondent No.1 and 2/driver and owner filed their written statement and denied the averments of rash and negligent driving and causing the accident by it.
It was pleaded that a criminal case was also registered against the driver of the appellant and therefore the driver and Insurance company of that vehicle was also a necessary party.
No damage was caused to the vehicle of the appellant by the vehicle of the respondent No.1 & 2.

On the date of incident, the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3.
4.
Respondent No.3/Insurance Company also filed its written statement and pleaded that the offending vehicle was not insured for third party property damage and was only for third party risk.
Hence, the appellant is not entitled for any compensation.

On the date of incident, respondent No.1/driver did not have valid and effective driving Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32514 license and the word being used in breach of terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.

The factum of rash and negligent driving was also denied and it was also denied that the appellant has spent any amount for repairing or any damage was caused to his vehicle and prayed for dismissal of the claim application.
5.
On the basis of the above broad pleadings of the parties, the learned Tribunal framed as many as six issues.

The issue No.1 is with regard to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle was decided as not proved, issue No.2 with regard to the complete damage of the vehicle of appellant is decided in positive.
Issue No.3 was with regard to contributory negligence, was held that the vehicle driven by the appellant's driver was negligent.
Issue with regard to violation of the policy was decided as not proved.
Issue No.5 & 6 with regard to amount of compensation was decided and not proved and relief and cost, the application was dismissed.
6. Shri Praveen Dhurander, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the finding with regard to issue No.1 is absolutely unjustified.

From the evidence on record, it is established that the driver of the offending vehicle respondent No.1 was negligent in causing the accident by which the vehicle of the appellant got damaged completely.

He submits that the finding with regard to issue No.2 has been decided in positive which goes to show that the accident has occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

He further submits that the FIR was lodged against the driver of the offending vehicle and he was charge sheeted therefore, applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur it cannot be said Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32514 that he was not negligent in causing the accident.

Alternatively, he submits that even if it is found that the entire negligence is not on the part of respondent No.1/driver, some amount to compensate the damages caused to the vehicle of the appellant ought to have been granted.
The finding with regard to issue No.3 of contributory negligence is also liable to be set aside.

He further submits that in view of the Vishnu Kumar Gupta vs Prakashchandra Yadav on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33730820/
2 above, the matter may be remitted back setting aside the findings as well as the impugned award.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Shri Hanuman Prasad Agrawal, learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company opposes the submission by contending that simply because the driver of the offending vehicle insured with the respondent No.3 was prosecuted for certain offences and charge sheet was filed, it would not automatically lead to prove the fact that he was negligent in causing the accident.
He further submits that the driver of the offending vehicle himself appeared before the learned Tribunal and deposed that the driver of the vehicle owned by the appellant was negligent.
The findings which have been recorded by the learned Tribunal is based upon proper appreciation of evidence and well merited and may not to be disturbed in this appeal.
He further submits that from the evidence on record it is established that a criminal case was also registered against the driver of the vehicle of the appellant.
He further submits that the policy was not covering the risk of third party property damage and was act only policy.
He submits that the driver of the damaged vehicle was not examined to substantiate that he was not negligent.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32514 records.
9.
From the evidence on record it is apparent that the accident had occurred on 26.02.2013 at about 1.30 pm.
Immediately thereafter at about 4.30 pm report was lodged and very categorically the driver of the offending vehicle CG-16A-1705 was named in the FIR.
From the criminal papers appended, it is apparent that the vehicle was also seized during the course of investigation and the damages which have been caused to the vehicle was also assessed.
The report was lodged by the driver of the appellant and there was not occasion for lodging this report and there was no occasion for the police to seize that vehicle and also to assess the damages.
10. It is well settled under the Motor Vehicle Act, strict compliance of of the evidence is not necessary.

It is a summary procedure and when the Tribunal while deciding the issue No.2, has given a finding that some damages have been caused therefore, in the opinion of this Court, ends of justice would be met if the matter is remitted back for deciding it afresh giving opportunities to the parties to lead evidence and amend pleadings.
The impugned award is set aside.
The matter is remanded back to the learned Tribunal for fresh decision making after giving opportunity to all the respondents to make pleadings, file documents, lead evidence, if any.
The learned Tribunal may consider the issue with regard to contributory negligence.
11. With this observation, the appeal is partly allowed.
The parties shall appear before the learned Tribunal on 22nd January 2024.
In case if any party fails to appear, the learned Tribunal shall issue notices of the application for their appearance before it.

This Court has Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32514 not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case and it would be upon the learned Tribunal to decide the application in accordance with law.
Sd/-
(Sachin Singh Rajput) Judge suguna Vishnu Kumar Gupta vs Prakashchandra Yadav on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33730820/
